title: A liquid takes the shape of its container and keeps its own volume
summary: A liquid takes the shape of its container, keeps a fixed volume, and shows a free surface where gravity acts.
body: NASA Glenn says molecular forces in a liquid are weaker than in a solid. A liquid will take the shape of its container with a free surface in a gravitational field. In microgravity, a liquid forms a ball inside a free surface. Regardless of gravity, a liquid has a fixed volume. That fixed volume is what separates it from a gas, which gives up its volume to the holder. The page does not time how fast anything pours.

sources.title: States of Matter
